_comment: Reviewed high/critical dependency advisories, consumed by scripts/audit-ratchet.mjs.
- An advisory NOT listed here fails the Security workflow. New debt is blocked.
- A listed advisory that no longer reproduces ALSO fails, so the list can only
shrink. That is what makes this a ratchet rather than an ignore-list.
- Every entry needs a `reason` stating the real exposure in THIS codebase and,
if the fix is deferred, the concrete blocker. 'Transitive' is not a reason.
State as of 2026-09-25: empty. The backlog that existed when the gate was built
(4 high in server, 1 in frontend, 3 in mobile) was fixed rather than accepted:
fast-uri 3.1.5->3.1.8, and the @tiptap/* tree unified on 3.31.3.

accepted.name: @expo/cli
accepted.reason: Build/dev tooling only; the flagged surface is its embedded code-signing verification (node-forge) used for OTA bundles, which this project never produces or validates. No fixed @expo/cli release as of expo 57.

accepted.name: @expo/code-signing-certificates
accepted.reason: Carrier of the vulnerable node-forge for OTA update signature checks. Same exposure note as node-forge: the app does not consume expo-updates, so the verifier never runs. Blocked upstream — no fixed release of the chain.

accepted.name: expo
accepted.reason: Flags the same node-forge chain via @expo/cli — npm's suggested fix (expo 44.0.6) is a six-major downgrade and wrong for RN 0.86. No real fix version exists; the vulnerable code path (OTA signing) is unused.

accepted.name: node-forge
accepted.reason: Only reachable through @expo/cli's OTA code-signing certificate verification (@expo/code-signing-certificates). The mobile app ships as a compiled APK/AAB — expo-updates is not a dependency and no OTA bundle signature is ever verified at runtime. No patched node-forge release exists (advisory range *). Unblocks when Expo's CLI chain upgrades node-forge.
